newsitem.title: FRANCE: HORSE RACING-FABRE IN STRONG BID FOR FRENCH DERBY.
newsitem.headline: HORSE RACING-FABRE IN STRONG BID FOR FRENCH DERBY.

text.p: Master trainer Andre Fabre has won virtually every top race in the European horse racing calendar and has a strong hand to capture the French Derby, which has eluded him so far, in the Chantilly classic on Sunday.
Fragrant Mix is unbeaten in three starts this term and has been saved for this race after trotting up in the Prix Noaille at Longchamp in April.
Fabre also goes to war with his Prix Greffulhe winner Peintre Celebre and his beautifully bred and progressive listed winner Arabian King.

Shaka, the Jean-Claude Rouget runner and 1996 Criterium de Saint-Cloud winner, is in dire need of a run after finishing third in the Noaille, three and a half lengths behind the very fit Fragrant Mix.
Shaka has since returned to his best, coming from off the pace to beat Pascal Barry's Oscar by a length in the Prix Hocquart here on May 3.
The Barry yard, which has won the French Derby twice before with Celtic Arms and Ragmar, is reopposing with Oscar.

There will be three visitors from abroad with English trainer Peter Chapple-Hyam's Voyagers Quest, a winner in France last term and seemingly superior to his compatriot Perfect Paradigm. They will be joined by the supplemented Irish colt Casey Tibbs.
Voyagers Quest won his only outing this term, the Thresher Classic Trial at Sandown in April, in handsome form.
Benny The Dip and Silver Patriarch, who then finished second and third, have both since won recognised English Derby trials in impressive style and are firm fancies for the Epsom classic on June 7.
